input.claim_text: Over the last two years a slow leak under the bathroom vanity rotted the floor and cabinet. We only noticed it last week. Estimated repair $7,800.

output.cause: slow bathroom vanity leakage over two years

input.query: Is gradual/slow leak causing rot over time covered or excluded?

input.query: gradual damage exclusion wear and tear rot resulting from continuous or gradual leaking

output.answer:
Based on the excerpts provided:

**Under "Accidental damage" cover, wear, tear, and rot are explicitly excluded.** Both the AAMI Building PDS and AAMI Contents PDS state that accidental damage cover does **not** extend to "loss or damage caused by: wear, tear, deterioration, rust, fading, rising damp, mould, mildew, corrosion, and rot" [AAMI Building PDS, page 70]; [AAMI Contents PDS, page 70].

**However, under the separate "Escape of liquid" insured event (Building PDS only, in the excerpts provided), gradual leaking is specifically covered**, subject to a visibility test:

> "Gradual loss or damage — We also cover loss or damage, caused by liquid escaping from any of [the listed sources — drains, sewage system, fixed pipes, water mains, fixed tanks, pools/spas, bath/sink/toilet/basin, fixed heating/cooling systems, fridge/freezer/dishwasher/washing machine, waterbed, or aquarium] that has occurred gradually when the loss or damage, that was occurring, wasn't easily visible to a reasonable person in the circumstances." [AAMI Building PDS, page 46]

This means gradual leaking from those specified sources can be covered under "Escape of liquid" even though general wear, tear, and rot are excluded from the "Accidental damage" section. The excerpts do not clarify whether resulting rot itself (as opposed to the liquid escape causing the damage) would be separately excluded once a valid Escape of liquid claim is established, and no excerpt for Contents PDS "Escape of liquid" wording was provided, so I cannot confirm whether the same gradual-leak cover applies to contents.

**Limitation of the excerpts:** No excerpt was provided showing an explicit interaction between the "Escape of liquid" gradual cover and the general wear/tear/rot exclusion (e.g., whether rot caused by a covered gradual leak is still payable). If you need that specific clarification, additional policy pages addressing exclusions within the "Escape of liquid" section itself would be needed.
